seoTitle: How to Compare Two Charts in TradingView
metaDescription: Learn how to compare two stocks, indices, or crypto pairs in TradingView using the Compare feature, overlay tool, and split screen layout.
intro: Whether you're checking correlation between two assets or analyzing relative strength, TradingView offers several ways to view charts side by side. This guide covers the Compare feature, symbol overlay, and split screen layout, along with tips on adjusting scale for accurate comparisons. It's aimed at traders and investors who want a clearer picture of how two instruments move together or apart.

steps.heading: Use the Compare feature
steps.body: Open the Compare tool in TradingView and add a second symbol to view it alongside your existing chart.

steps.heading: Try the overlay method
steps.body: Overlay one symbol directly on top of another on the same chart to visually compare their price movements.

steps.heading: Use split screen layout
steps.body: Set up a split screen layout so each symbol has its own dedicated chart panel for side-by-side viewing.

steps.heading: Adjust scale for accurate comparison
steps.body: Fine-tune the price scale, especially when comparing assets with very different price ranges, to make the comparison meaningful.

steps.heading: Apply tips for correlation and relative strength analysis
steps.body: Look at how closely the two assets move together, and how far apart they diverge, to inform decisions like pair trading or sector rotation.

faq.question: What's the difference between the Compare feature and overlay?
faq.answer: The Compare feature typically adds a second symbol on a separate scale for reference, while overlay places it directly on the same price axis as your original chart.

faq.question: Can I compare more than two symbols at once?
faq.answer: TradingView generally allows multiple symbols to be added for comparison, though readability can suffer if you add too many at once.

faq.question: Why is scale important when comparing two charts?
faq.answer: If two assets have very different price ranges, an unadjusted scale can make the comparison visually misleading, so scaling appropriately is important.

faq.question: Is split screen better than overlay for comparison?
faq.answer: It depends on your goal; split screen gives each asset its own clear view, while overlay is better for directly seeing how closely they move together.
